note: Who Instagram shows a small finance reel to. Most views of a small account's reel come from non-followers whose recent viewing looks like the reel's topic, plus a broad test batch. Weights sum to 1; rebuild from the account's follower and reach demographics once insights are readable.

personas.who: Jay, 19, UK uni student. Opened a trading app last month, watches money TikToks, wants quick wins. Swipes on anything that feels like a lecture or an ad.
Tyler, 16, US high schooler. Gaming and meme pages; stocks only through meme-stock jokes. Stops for absurd, funny or game-like things, gone in a second if it looks like school.
Diego, 30, Spain, crypto and options gambler. Loves dramatic pumps and crashes, big numbers, 'I lost everything' stories. Bored by slow explanations.
Lena, 23, Germany, marketing assistant. Follows personal-finance creators, has never traded. Wants simple, clear, friendly explainers; leaves if jargon shows up early.
Priya, 27, India/US, software engineer, index-fund investor. Curious about charts but allergic to hype and get-rich-quick; respects precise, honest content.
Marcus, 34, US, part-time futures day trader who knows technical analysis well. Skeptical of beginner content, comments when something is wrong, saves genuinely good setups.
Sam, 45, Australia, dad with ETFs, scrolls in the evening. Likes practical lessons he can use; dislikes fast, loud edits.
Omar, 26, Canada, gamer who loves strategy games, puzzles and quizzes. Will play along with a 'guess what happens next' challenge and comment his answer if it's quick.
Chloe, 21, US, scrolls for entertainment, no interest in finance. Instagram tests reels on people like her; she stops only for something surprising, funny or visually striking.
Hannah, 38, UK nurse, anxious about money, has never invested. Stops for relatable money stakes, leaves at charts with no explanation.
Ben, 29, Ireland, follows meme pages and finance memes (wallstreetbets humour). Shares things to friends' group chat when they're funny or savage.
Aisha, 24, Nigeria/UK, finance graduate working at a bank. Spots inaccuracies, saves good educational content, shares useful tips with colleagues.
Kai, 22, already follows @memestreetgame and has played its Daily Chart twice. Sees the brand header and knows what to expect; watches if the reel promises something new.
